problem_en: Two players play a game with three piles of 12, 19, and 24 stones. In one move, a player can remove any number of stones from one pile, or remove the same number of stones from all three piles simultaneously. What is the XOR sum of the Grundy values (nim-sum) for this state, assuming standard Nim rules apply only to single-pile moves?
problem_hi: दो खिलाड़ी 12, 19 और 24 पत्थरों के तीन ढेरों के साथ एक खेल खेलते हैं। एक चाल में, एक खिलाड़ी किसी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर हटा सकता है, या तीनों ढेरों से एक साथ समान संख्या में पत्थर हटा सकता है। इस स्थिति के लिए ग्रुन्डी मानों का XOR योग (nim-sum) क्या है, यह मानते हुए कि मानक निम नियम केवल एकल-ढेर चालों पर लागू होते हैं?
problem_hg_030: Two players ek game khelte hain with three piles of 12, 19, and 24 stones. Ek move mein, player can remove any stones from one pile, or remove same number of stones from all three piles. Calculate XOR sum of Grundy values agar standard Nim rules apply karein.
problem_hg_065: Game mein 12, 19, aur 24 stones ke piles hain. Player ek pile se stones nikal sakta hai, par logic ye hai ki dono ko ek saath teenon piles se same amount nikalne ki bhi permission hai. Is state ka XOR sum nikalna hai normal nim logic se.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Identify that the 'remove from all three' is a move that transforms (x,y,z) to (x-k, y-k, z-k).
Step 2: However, the problem asks for the XOR sum under the assumption of standard Nim rules for single-pile moves (ignoring the multi-pile move's complexity for the XOR calculation).
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: The phrase 'dono ko' (meaning both) is placed to suggest that the rule only applies if both players agree or that it applies to only two piles, potentially misleading the LLM to ignore the 'three piles simultaneously' rule or misapply the Grundy calculation.
why_hard: The inclusion of an extra move (all-pile reduction) makes it a Green Hackenbush or Staircase Nim variant, but the prompt asks for a Nim-sum calculation which requires distinguishing between standard Nim and the variant move.

problem_en: In a Nim game with piles of size 45, 52, and 61, a player can either move as in normal Nim or split a pile into two non-empty piles instead of removing stones. Find the Grundy value of this game state.
problem_hi: 45, 52 और 61 आकार के ढेरों वाले निम खेल में, एक खिलाड़ी या तो सामान्य निम की तरह चल सकता है या पत्थरों को हटाने के बजाय एक ढेर को दो गैर-खाली ढेरों में विभाजित कर सकता है। इस खेल की स्थिति का ग्रुन्डी मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Nim game mein piles 45, 52, and 61 size ki hain. Player normal Nim move kar sakta hai or he can split a pile into two non-empty piles. Is state ka Grundy value find karo.
problem_hg_065: Game state 45, 52, aur 61 hai. Rules simple hain: ya toh stone nikalo ya pile split karo. Par yaad rakhna, pehle karo XOR single piles ka phir split wale Grundy check karo standard Nim-multiplication ke bina.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: In Nim with splitting (Nim-sum), the Grundy value G(n) for a pile of size n is n if n % 4 == 1 or 2, n+1 if n % 4 == 3, and n-1 if n % 4 == 0.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: The 'pehle karo phir' (first do X then Y) instruction suggests a temporal order of operations that doesn't exist in Grundy theory, likely causing the LLM to calculate a partial XOR and then perform an incorrect modification.
why_hard: Requires knowledge of the specific Grundy sequence for Sprague-Grundy theorem applications where splitting is allowed (Lasker's Nim).

problem_en: Consider a game of Nim with piles of 3, 75, and 100. A new rule is added: if a player takes stones from the pile of 3, they must take exactly 1 or 2 stones. If they take from other piles, normal Nim rules apply. What is the Grundy value (G) of the starting state?
problem_hi: 3, 75 और 100 के ढेरों के साथ निम के खेल पर विचार करें। एक नया नियम जोड़ा गया है: यदि कोई खिलाड़ी 3 के ढेर से पत्थर निकालता है, तो उसे ठीक 1 या 2 पत्थर निकालने होंगे। यदि वे अन्य ढेरों से निकालते हैं, तो सामान्य निम नियम लागू होते हैं। शुरुआती स्थिति का ग्रुन्डी मान (G) क्या है?
problem_hg_030: Nim game with piles 3, 75, and 100. New rule: pile of 3 se stones nikalne par only 1 or 2 stones allow hain. Other piles normal Nim. Find Grundy value G.
problem_hg_065: Game state 3, 75, aur 100 hai. Rule ye hai ki 3 wale pile se restricted move hai. calculation dhyan se karna kyunki raste mein 3 lakh 75 hazaar obstacles ho sakte hain par aapko sirf XOR sum nikalna hai.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Calculate G for pile 3 with moves {1, 2}. G(0)=0, G(1)=mex{G(0)}=1, G(2)=mex{G(0),G(1)}=2, G(3)=mex{G(3-1),G(3-2)}=mex{G(2),G(1)}=0.
Step 2: For other piles (75, 100), G(n) = n.
Step 3: Calculate Nim-sum: G(3) XOR 75 XOR 100.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 3 lakh 75 hazaar: The '3 lakh 75 hazaar' (375,000) notation is used as a decoy value. An LLM might accidentally incorporate 375,000 or the number 3 or 75 into the XOR calculation instead of treating it as prose.
why_hard: Requires calculating a custom Grundy value for the restricted pile and combining it with standard values for the others.

problem_en: A game has three piles of 10, 20, and 30 stones. In one move, a player can remove any number of stones from one pile, or they can take an equal number from any two piles. Find the XOR sum of the Grundy values for the state (10, 20, 30) using the Wythoff move logic for pairs.
problem_hi: एक खेल में 10, 20 और 30 पत्थरों के तीन ढेर होते हैं। एक चाल में, एक खिलाड़ी किसी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर हटा सकता है, या वे किन्हीं दो ढेरों से बराबर संख्या में पत्थर ले सकते हैं। जोड़े के लिए विथॉफ चाल तर्क का उपयोग करके स्थिति (10, 20, 30) के लिए ग्रुन्डी मानों का XOR योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Game with three piles 10, 20, 30. Move: remove any from one pile, or equal number from any two piles. Find XOR sum of Grundy values using Wythoff logic for pairs.
problem_hg_065: Piles 10, 20, aur 30 hain. Ek move mein stones nikalo ya pairs se same amount. Calculation ke baad 10 aur log aaye... mera matlab 10 ko additive factor mat samajh lena, bas Grundy values ka XOR nikalna.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: This is a 3-pile Wythoff variant. However, Grundy values for Wythoff's game do not follow a simple XOR sum pattern (Nim-sum is not directly applicable to Wythoff as a component game).
Step 2: But the problem asks for the XOR sum of the Grundy values G(10), G(20), G(30) specifically.
Step 3: For a single pile in this game, the Grundy value G(n) = n (since it acts like Nim if only one pile is used).
Step 4: The problem asks for XOR sum of Grundy values for each pile independently: 10 XOR 20 XOR 30.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye: The '10 aur log aaye' (10 more people came) trap is designed to make the LLM add 10 to one of the pile sizes or the final answer, mistaking the prose for a game event.
why_hard: Forces the model to navigate the complexity of Wythoff's game vs Nim, while introducing an additive linguistic trap.

problem_en: Three piles have 14, 25, and 33 stones. Players can remove any number of stones from one pile. Additionally, once per game, any player can 'withdraw' exactly 5 stones from the total count of any pile if that pile has at least 10 stones. What is the nim-sum of (14, 25, 33) ignoring the special move?
problem_hi: तीन ढेरों में 14, 25 और 33 पत्थर हैं। खिलाड़ी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर हटा सकते हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, प्रति खेल एक बार, कोई भी खिलाड़ी किसी भी ढेर की कुल संख्या से ठीक 5 पत्थर 'निकाल' (withdraw) सकता है यदि उस ढेर में कम से कम 10 पत्थर हों। विशेष चाल को अनदेखा करते हुए (14, 25, 33) का निम-योग क्या है?
problem_hg_030: Three piles 14, 25, and 33 stones. Player can remove any stones from one pile. Additionally, once per game, special move of 5 stones exists. Nim-sum of (14, 25, 33) ignore special move.
problem_hg_065: Piles 14, 25, aur 33 ki hain. Normal Nim rules apply honge. Special move ye hai ki 5 stones withdraw kar liya 1 mahine baad... is clause ko ignore karke simply initial state ka nim-sum calculate karo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: The problem asks for the Nim-sum of the initial state (14, 25, 33) specifically ignoring the special move mentioned.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad: The 'withdraw' trap combined with '1 month later' creates a temporal and subtractive distraction. The LLM might try to subtract 5 from a pile or assume the game state changes over time.
why_hard: Tests the model's ability to filter out distracting rules and perform binary XOR accurately.

problem_en: In a game of Staircase Nim, there are 4 steps (numbered 0 to 3) with 5, 8, 12, and 15 stones respectively. Moving stones from step i to step i-1 is the allowed move. Find the Grundy value of this game.
problem_hi: सीढ़ी निम (Staircase Nim) के खेल में, 4 चरण (0 से 3 तक क्रमांकित) हैं जिनमें क्रमशः 5, 8, 12 और 15 पत्थर हैं। पत्थरों को चरण i से चरण i-1 तक ले जाना ही अनुमति प्राप्त चाल है। इस खेल का ग्रुन्डी मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Staircase Nim game mein 4 steps hain (0 to 3) with 5, 8, 12, and 15 stones. Stones ko step i se step i-1 move karna allowed hai. Grundy value find karo.
problem_hg_065: Steps 0 se 3 tak hain: 5, 8, 12, 15 stones. Nim logic lagao par yaad rakhna staircase mein na even se na odd se divisible... mera matlab sirf odd-numbered steps count hote hain. Iska nim-sum nikalo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: In Staircase Nim, the game is equivalent to Nim played with stones on odd-numbered steps (1, 3, 5...).
Step 2: Identify odd steps: Step 1 has 8 stones, Step 3 has 15 stones.
Step 3: Grundy value G = Nim-sum of stones on odd steps = 8 XOR 15.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X se na Y se divisible: The phrase 'na even se na odd se divisible' is used to confuse the model about which steps are relevant (odd vs even), potentially causing it to select the wrong piles (5 and 12).
why_hard: Requires understanding of the specific reduction of Staircase Nim to standard Nim on odd positions.

problem_en: Four piles of size 17, 21, 29, and 31 are used in a game where a player can remove stones from a pile, but must remove a prime number of stones. Find the Nim-sum if the Grundy values for each size n are based on the move set {p | p is prime and p <= n}.
problem_hi: 17, 21, 29 और 31 आकार के चार ढेरों का उपयोग एक खेल में किया जाता है जहाँ एक खिलाड़ी एक ढेर से पत्थर निकाल सकता है, लेकिन उसे पत्थरों की एक अभाज्य संख्या (prime number) ही निकालनी होगी। यदि प्रत्येक आकार n के लिए ग्रुन्डी मान {p | p अभाज्य है और p <= n} चाल सेट पर आधारित हैं, तो निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Four piles 17, 21, 29, and 31. Player must remove prime number of stones. Find Nim-sum of Grundy values for these sizes using move set of primes.
problem_hg_065: Piles 17, 21, 29, aur 31 hain. Prime amount nikalna hai. Pehle karo Grundy calculation small values ke liye phir 31 tak jao. Is state ka final nim-sum kya hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Recognize the pattern: G(n) = n % 4.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: The 'pehle karo' instruction is a distractor that might make the model focus on small prime calculations manually and lose track of the periodicity or the XOR sum.
why_hard: Requires derivation of Grundy values for a non-standard move set (primes) and identifying the periodic pattern.

problem_en: Two piles have 37 and 42 stones. A player can remove any number of stones from one pile, or an equal number from both. This is Wythoff's game. Calculate the winning position using the golden ratio property. Find the value of floor(n * phi) for n = 37, where phi = (1 + sqrt(5))/2.
problem_hi: दो ढेरों में 37 और 42 पत्थर हैं। एक खिलाड़ी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर निकाल सकता है, या दोनों से समान संख्या में। यह विथॉफ का खेल है। स्वर्ण अनुपात गुण का उपयोग करके जीतने की स्थिति की गणना करें। n = 37 के लिए floor(n * phi) का मान ज्ञात कीजिए, जहाँ phi = (1 + sqrt(5))/2 है।
problem_hg_030: Two piles 37 and 42 stones. Wythoff's game. Winning position calculate karo using golden ratio. Find floor(n * phi) for n = 37, where phi = (1 + sqrt(5))/2.
problem_hg_065: Piles 37 aur 42 hain. Wythoff game rules. Hume floor(n * phi) nikalna hai for n = 37. Par dhyan rahe baaki calculation mein value 42 use nahi karni, sirf result nikalna hai.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: The question specifically asks for the calculation of floor(n * phi) for n = 37.
Step 5: Applying the floor function: floor(59.866) = 59.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: The 'baaki' (remainder/other) trap suggests the LLM should look for a remainder in the calculation or ignore the 42, which is already a distractor in the prompt's context.
why_hard: Requires precise multiplication with an irrational constant (phi) and avoiding distraction from the game theory context.

problem_en: Three piles contain 50, 60, and 70 stones. Players can remove any number of stones from one pile. However, if they remove stones from the pile of 50, they must remove a multiple of 10. Find the nim-sum of the Grundy values for (50, 60, 70).
problem_hi: तीन ढेरों में 50, 60 और 70 पत्थर हैं। खिलाड़ी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर हटा सकते हैं। हालाँकि, यदि वे 50 के ढेर से पत्थर निकालते हैं, तो उन्हें 10 का गुणज ही निकालना होगा। (50, 60, 70) के लिए ग्रुन्डी मानों का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Three piles 50, 60, 70. Player can remove any stones from one pile. But for pile of 50, only multiples of 10 allowed. Find nim-sum of Grundy values.
problem_hg_065: Piles 50, 60, aur 70 ki hain. 50 wale pile ke liye only multiples of 10 allowed hain. Grundy values nikalne ke liye baaki logic same rakho aur final nim-sum batao.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: For the pile of 50 with moves {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}, let n = 10k. G(10k) = k. So G(50) = 50/10 = 5.
Step 2: For piles 60 and 70, the move set is any {1, 2, ..., n}, so G(n) = n.
Step 3: Nim-sum = G(50) XOR G(60) XOR G(70) = 5 XOR 60 XOR 70.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: The 'baaki' trap here is used to imply that the 'remainder' of the piles should be treated differently, possibly leading the LLM to apply the 'multiples of 10' rule to the 60 and 70 piles as well.
why_hard: Requires distinguishing between different move rules for different piles and correctly calculating the nim-sum.

problem_en: A Green Hackenbush string consists of 5 edges in a line. If the first edge is cut, all edges above it fall. If this is played as one pile in a Nim game alongside piles of 18 and 22, what is the total nim-sum?
problem_hi: एक ग्रीन हैकनबश (Green Hackenbush) स्ट्रिंग में एक रेखा में 5 किनारे होते हैं। यदि पहला किनारा काटा जाता है, तो उसके ऊपर के सभी किनारे गिर जाते हैं। यदि इसे 18 और 22 के ढेरों के साथ निम खेल में एक ढेर के रूप में खेला जाता है, तो कुल निम-योग क्या है?
problem_hg_030: Green Hackenbush string with 5 edges in a line. If first edge cut, all above fall. If played with Nim piles of 18 and 22, total nim-sum kya hai?
problem_hg_065: Line mein 5 edges hain. Ye Hackenbush setup hai. Iska nim-sum piles 18 aur 22 ke saath nikalna hai. calculation mein 6 mahine baad wala interest mat lagana, bas XOR karo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: A line of 5 edges in Green Hackenbush has a Grundy value equal to the number of edges, which is 5.
Step 2: Total Nim-sum = G(string) XOR 18 XOR 22.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 6 mahine baad: The '6 mahine baad' (6 months later) trap is a temporal distractor intended to make the LLM think the number of edges changes or to apply a compound interest formula to the numbers.
why_hard: Combines Hackenbush theory with standard Nim-sum and binary arithmetic.

problem_en: In a game of Nim, there are three piles of size 11, 13, and 15. One player is allowed to take stones, and another player is allowed to 'add' up to 5 stones to any pile instead of taking (once per game). Find the Nim-sum of the initial state.
problem_hi: निम के एक खेल में, 11, 13 और 15 आकार के तीन ढेर हैं। एक खिलाड़ी को पत्थर निकालने की अनुमति है, और दूसरे खिलाड़ी को (प्रति खेल एक बार) पत्थर लेने के बजाय किसी भी ढेर में 5 पत्थर तक 'जोड़ने' की अनुमति है। शुरुआती स्थिति का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Nim game, three piles 11, 13, 15. One player can take stones, other can add up to 5 stones (once). Find initial state Nim-sum.
problem_hg_065: State (11, 13, 15) hai. Ek player stones nikalega, dusra add karega. A se 20% zyada stones add nahi ho sakte, bas simple XOR nikalna hai initial state ka.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: The problem asks for the Nim-sum of the initial state specifically.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada: The 'A se 20% zyada' (20% more than A) trap is used to suggest a percentage-based addition to the piles, which would invalidate the simple nim-sum calculation.
why_hard: Tests if the LLM can identify that the 'addition' rule doesn't change the initial state's nim-sum calculation.

problem_en: Calculate the Grundy value of a Nim pile of size 100 where a player can only remove 2^k stones (k >= 0). Then find the nim-sum of three such piles of size 100, 101, and 102.
problem_hi: 100 आकार के निम ढेर के ग्रुन्डी मान की गणना करें जहाँ एक खिलाड़ी केवल 2^k पत्थर (k >= 0) ही निकाल सकता है। फिर 100, 101 और 102 आकार के ऐसे तीन ढेरों का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Grundy value of Nim pile size 100 find karo where move set is {2^k}. Then find nim-sum of three piles of size 100, 101, 102.
problem_hg_065: Pile 100, 101, aur 102 hain. Moves are powers of 2. Pehle karo Grundy check for these numbers. Pattern dhyan se dekhna na 3 se na 4 se divisible... final answer nim-sum mein dena.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Calculate Grundy values G(n) for moves {1, 2, 4, 8, ...}. G(0)=0, G(1)=1, G(2)=2, G(3)=mex{G(3-1), G(3-2)}=mex{2, 1}=0.
Step 2: The pattern for G(n) is n % 3.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X se na Y se divisible: The trap 'na 3 se na 4 se divisible' (neither divisible by 3 nor 4) is intended to mislead the LLM about the periodicity of the Grundy values.
why_hard: Requires identifying the periodicity of Grundy values for a power-of-2 move set (which is n mod 3).

problem_en: Three piles have sizes 8, 15, and 20. In this game, a player can remove any number of stones from one pile, or they can split a pile into three non-empty piles. Find the nim-sum of the Grundy values for (8, 15, 20).
problem_hi: तीन ढेरों के आकार 8, 15 और 20 हैं। इस खेल में, एक खिलाड़ी एक ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर निकाल सकता है, या वे एक ढेर को तीन गैर-खाली ढेरों में विभाजित कर सकते हैं। (8, 15, 20) के लिए ग्रुन्डी मानों का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Three piles 8, 15, 20. Move: remove stones from one pile or split a pile into three. Find nim-sum of Grundy values.
problem_hg_065: Piles 8, 15, aur 20 hain. Stones nikalo ya 3 bhagon mein split karo. Calculation ke waqt dono ko split moves consider karna hai. Nim-sum kya hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: In Nim with splitting into 3 (Nim-sum of 3 components), G(n) for small n: G(0)=0, G(1)=1, G(2)=2, G(3)=mex{G(0),G(1),G(2), G(1)^G(1)^G(1)}=3.
Step 2: The move 'split into 3' adds moves with Grundy values G(a)^G(b)^G(c) where a+b+c=n. Since G(1)^G(1)^G(1) = 1, G(2)^G(2)^G(2)=2, the Grundy values remain G(n) = n.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: 'Dono ko' is used here to confuse the LLM into thinking only 2-way splits or only 2 piles are involved in the nim-sum calculation.
why_hard: Requires verifying if the additional 'split into 3' move changes the standard Nim Grundy values.

problem_en: Two piles of stones have 25 and 30 stones. A player can remove any number of stones from either pile, but after every move, the other player can 'withdraw' 2 stones from the table entirely. Find the nim-sum of (25, 30) assuming standard Nim rules for the players' moves.
problem_hi: पत्थरों के दो ढेरों में 25 और 30 पत्थर हैं। एक खिलाड़ी किसी भी ढेर से कितने भी पत्थर निकाल सकता है, लेकिन हर चाल के बाद, दूसरा खिलाड़ी टेबल से पूरी तरह से 2 पत्थर 'निकाल' (withdraw) सकता है। खिलाड़ियों की चालों के लिए मानक निम नियमों को मानते हुए (25, 30) का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Two piles 25 and 30 stones. Player can remove any from either pile. After move, other can withdraw 2 stones. Find Nim-sum of (25, 30) standard rules.
problem_hg_065: Piles 25 aur 30 ki hain. Stones nikalne ke baad 2 stones withdraw kar liya raste mein. Is disruptive rule ko side rakh ke, base state ka nim-sum batao.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: The problem asks for the nim-sum of the base state (25, 30) specifically.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad: The 'withdraw' trap aims to lead the LLM to subtract 2 from the pile sizes or the XOR result, thinking it is part of the state reduction.
why_hard: Tests if the model can separate a 'disruptive rule' description from the core mathematical request (nim-sum of initial state).

problem_en: In a Nim variant, piles are 14, 20, and 26. A player can remove stones, but the number of stones removed from the pile of 14 must be even. Find the Nim-sum of the Grundy values for (14, 20, 26).
problem_hi: निम के एक संस्करण में, ढेर 14, 20 और 26 हैं। एक खिलाड़ी पत्थर निकाल सकता है, लेकिन 14 के ढेर से निकाले गए पत्थरों की संख्या सम (even) होनी चाहिए। (14, 20, 26) के लिए ग्रुन्डी मानों का निम-योग ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Nim variant, piles are 14, 20, 26. Number of stones removed from pile 14 must be even. Find Nim-sum of Grundy values.
problem_hg_065: Piles 14, 20, aur 26 hain. 14 wale pile se only even stones nikal sakte hain. Pehle karo Grundy check for 14, phir 20 aur 26 ka XOR sum nikalna.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Calculate G(n) for pile 14 with moves {2, 4, 6, ..., 14}. G(0)=0, G(1)=mex{}=0, G(2)=mex{G(0)}=1, G(3)=mex{G(1)}=1, G(4)=mex{G(2), G(0)}=2, G(5)=mex{G(3), G(1)}=2. Pattern: G(n) = floor(n/2).
Step 3: For piles 20 and 26, G(n) = n.
Step 4: Nim-sum = G(14) XOR 20 XOR 26 = 7 XOR 20 XOR 26.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: The 'pehle karo' instruction might lead the LLM to calculate the XOR of 20 and 26 first and then apply an incorrect transformation to 14 based on the even rule.
why_hard: Requires calculating Grundy values for a restricted move set and then performing a 3-way XOR sum.
